nightly-evals-bot: ALERT — enwiki_retrieval nightly: recall@100 dropped 6.2% (0.912 -> 0.855) vs baseline. Affected artifacts: reranker=v2.6, embed_model=encoder-quant-v2. Full diff: https://internal.ci/nightly/1795432105 :warning:
Anya Patel: ugh, saw a couple failing prompt sets in the dashboard, can reproduce locally on a few queries
Samir Chen: I pushed reranker v2.6 yesterday — only change was a small margin rescale and updated tokenizer config. Not sure that explains recall drop at retrieval stage?
Marta Lopez: we also promoted encoder-quant-v2 to canary for 10% of traffic at 22:00 UTC last night. Could be embedding drift from quantization.
Kai Nguyen: quick hypothesis: quantized encoder changed embedding norms/topk ordering. Can we compute topk overlap vs baseline for the enwiki sample?
Anya Patel: running quick overlap now on the nightly dump, will paste numbers in a sec
Samir Chen: also check reranker calibration numbers — margin rescale might boost reranker scores differently and change rerank recall metrics. But primary retrieval recall drop suggests upstream embedding issue.
Anya Patel: (results) topk@100 overlap vs baseline = 0.67 on sampled queries. baseline overlap normally ~0.92. mean L2 norm delta = -0.18. That seems significant.
Marta Lopez: oh that's big. encoder-quant-v2 must be shifting vector magnitudes. Did quantization script change per-channel scales?
Kai Nguyen: paste command I used:
```bash
python infra/tools/compare_topk.py \
  --baseline gs://redwood-nightlies/enwiki/encoder-fp16/embeddings.npy \
  --candidate gs://redwood-nightlies/enwiki/encoder-quant-v2/embeddings.npy \
  --k 100 --out metrics.json
```
Samir Chen: thanks. I also pulled a few sample queries where reranker used to surface gold doc but now topk misses gold entirely. Looks like the gold doc dropped out of top500 for some queries.
Anya Patel: repro sample (query id 4421): baseline top5 ids = [1123, 778, 55, 990, 34] candidate top5 = [990, 34, 7845, 1123, 5562] — order and set changed a lot.
Marta Lopez: probable root cause: quantization scales were computed on a shorter calibration dataset (subset of wiki) and we missed tail tokens. I can re-run calibration with full corpus.
Kai Nguyen: short-term mitigation: revert canary roll and pin embed model to encoder-fp16 for retrieval path. Then re-evaluate reranker metrics.
Samir Chen: agree. Also add a quick guard in the rollout pipeline: require topk overlap >= 0.9 for retrieval candidates before promoting quantized encoders.
Anya Patel: I can open rollout revert PR and trigger rollback.
deploy-bot: started rollback: revert embed model for retrieval pipelines from encoder-quant-v2 -> encoder-fp16 (canary traffic 0% -> 100% revert in progress)
Samir Chen: after revert, re-run nightly eval locally on the same sample to confirm recovery.
nightly-evals-bot: NOTE — we ran a one-off eval after revert: recall@100 returned to 0.913 (within noise).
Julia Park: should we add an eval that checks embedding L2 distribution drift (mean+std) and topk overlap thresholds? Happy to add to the nightly suite.
Marta Lopez: yes please. I'll re-run quantization calibration with the full corpus and then produce a small A/B test comparing topk overlap, norm stats, and downstream reranker AUC before we re-promote.
Kai Nguyen: also add a small synthetic test that forces tail token coverage in calibration. Put results in PR template so we don't miss it next time.
Anya Patel: filing a short incident note in /incidents with root cause hypothesis = encoder quantization calibration on partial corpus. Will attach numeric diffs and sample queries.
Samir Chen: thanks everyone. Follow-ups: Marta to re-calibrate + canary plan, Julia to add drift checks to nightly evals, Anya to doc incident.
Marta Lopez: will do. ETA for re-calibration and canary re-promote: ~6 hours after calibration finishes.
Anya Patel: marking this thread resolved for now since revert is done and recall recovered. Will reopen if new regressions show up. :white_check_mark:
